questions.name: internet-to-web-https
questions.why: IGW maps the public IP one to one; acl-0public rule 100 lets 443 in, rule 100 out lets the reply to 1024-65535 out; rtb-0public routes 0.0.0.0/0 back to the IGW

questions.name: internet-to-web-ssh
questions.why: NACL rules are evaluated lowest number first; 22 is allowed only from 192.0.2.0/24, so the * rule denies it before any security group is asked

questions.name: office-to-web-ssh
questions.why: acl-0public rule 110 and sg-0web both allow 22 from 192.0.2.0/24

questions.name: internet-to-db
questions.why: db has no public IPv4 address; an internet gateway only accepts traffic for a public IP mapped to an interface

questions.name: web-to-db
questions.why: local route; sg-0db references sg-0web, which matches web's private IP; acl-0private rule 110 out allows the reply to 10.0.1.0/24

questions.name: web-to-db-ssh
questions.why: acl-0private allows only 5432 in from 10.0.1.0/24; the * rule denies 22

questions.name: worker-to-internet
questions.why: worker sits in a public subnet but has no public IPv4 address; the IGW has nothing to translate its private address to

questions.name: web-to-internet
questions.why: web's Linux client ports 32768-60999 fall inside acl-0public rule 120 (32768-65535)

questions.name: batch-to-internet
questions.why: a NAT gateway uses source ports 1024-65535; acl-0public copies the 32768-65535 example range, so replies to NAT ports 1024-32767 hit the * rule

questions.name: batch-to-s3
questions.why: the prefix list route to the gateway endpoint is more specific than 0.0.0.0/0, so S3 traffic skips the NAT gateway

questions.name: etl-to-db
questions.why: the request is allowed (acl-0private rule 105, sg-0db 10.1.0.0/16) but NACLs are stateless and acl-0private has no outbound rule for replies to 10.1.0.0/16

questions.name: etl-to-web
questions.why: rtb-0analytics routes only 10.0.2.0/24 over the peering connection

questions.name: web-to-etl
questions.why: rtb-0public has no peering route, so 10.1.1.40 matches 0.0.0.0/0 to the IGW, which drops private destinations

questions.name: batch-to-ldaps
questions.why: sg-0ldap allows 636 only from sg-0batch, and tgw-0core has security group referencing support off

questions.name: batch-to-ldap
questions.why: 172.16.0.0/12 to the transit gateway, a CIDR rule in sg-0ldap, and rtb-0legacy routes 10.0.0.0/8 back through the same transit gateway

questions.name: db-to-internet-dns
questions.why: sg-0db's only outbound rule is tcp 443; security groups are allow-only

questions.name: internet-to-report
questions.why: report has an Elastic IP but lives in a subnet whose 0.0.0.0/0 points at the NAT gateway, so the reply never leaves through the IGW
